body:
Ethan Park: need to lock down the feature flagging plan for incident-bot v2 before we open beta. goal is safe rollout + instant rollback. can we align today on (a) what flags exist, (b) cohort targeting, (c) rollback criteria + who can flip.

Miles Thornton: +1. we have v2 output behind a single env var in staging right now, but for prod we should do proper flag(s). also we need per-card gating because config diff is the riskiest.

Mina Haddad: pls don’t do “one big switch” only. routing/saturation cards are low-ish risk, config diff is high risk + permissions sensitive.

Benji Okafor: agreed. suggestion: a top-level `incident_bot.v2.enabled` kill switch + subflags:
- `incident_bot.v2.card.deploy_context`
- `incident_bot.v2.card.config_diff`
- `incident_bot.v2.card.saturation_signals`
- `incident_bot.v2.card.error_budget_links`
- `incident_bot.v2.slack.interactive_actions` (modals/pagination)
Each card should no-op cleanly if disabled (don’t show empty blocks).

Dylan Brooks: +1. also a separate safety flag for “live queries” vs “links only”. i.e. `incident_bot.v2.telemetry.live_queries` so we can fall back to cached + deep links if telemetry is melting.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE side: yes please. during incidents we want a kill switch that reduces bot load, not just hides the UI.

Ravi Menon: +1 on “links only” mode. in a partial outage, the bot should respond fast w/ cached context + console links. also we should explicitly define degraded mode as part of the rollout plan.

Devon Price: implementation detail: slack rendering layer can treat each card as a plugin keyed off the flags. kill switch is checked first; then each card checks its own flag; then the “live_queries” flag controls whether card does API calls or just prints links + last cached timestamp.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: permissions angle: config diff card must be guarded by BOTH (1) feature flag and (2) authz scope. no scenario where enabling flag accidentally lets everyone see tenant config diffs.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: also prefer a separate flag like `incident_bot.v2.card.config_diff.render_in_slack` vs `incident_bot.v2.card.config_diff.collect_only`. we might want to collect for internal logs / context completeness but not render until we’ve validated redaction.

Miles Thornton: good point. we can do 2 steps:
- phase 1: collect + redact + store (internal, access-controlled), Slack shows “Config changed? yes/no + link to Console diff”
- phase 2: render safe diff snippets in Slack for authorized users

Mina Haddad: cohort targeting: what’s the plan? only SRE rotation initially? also which channels? would like to avoid random eng channels getting spammed.

Rafael Mendes: beta cohort proposal from SRE thread was: SRE primary oncall rotation only, plus incident commanders (IC) in #incidents. Keep it limited to us-east + eu-west first (most common) and not dedicated/private on day 1.

Aisha Bello: for alerts/SLO links: let’s gate `error_budget_links` to the same cohort initially; if those links are wrong it’s confusing (and it’ll cause people to distrust the bot).

Ethan Park: ok targeting dimensions we can support:
- by Slack channel: only `#incidents` and `#eng-oncall` threads
- by user group: `@sre-oncall` + `@incident-commander` (if we can resolve)
- by environment: prod only after staging burn-in
- by region/service: if needed, but might be too complex

Devon Price: channel targeting is easiest. user group targeting depends on Slack APIs and caching group membership; doable but adds failure modes.

Miles Thornton: can we do: channel targeting + allowlist of “beta rotations” by oncall schedule (PagerDuty)?

Ravi Menon: i’d avoid hard dep on PD for v0. just channel-based + manual allowlist of Slack user IDs for beta. keep simple.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 to simple allowlist. plus: separate “who can flip flags” from “who can see data”. flag flipping should be limited to SRE + platform leads; data view should remain controlled by scopes.

Benji Okafor: where do flags live? prefer our internal Flagger service (same as console rollouts). it supports percentage + allowlist and has audit logs.

Ethan Park: yes, Flagger. we’ll define ownership: Platform Control Plane owns the flags; SRE has permissions to toggle kill switch + live_queries. Product doesn’t need direct toggle rights in prod.

Rafael Mendes: can we have a documented “rollback playbook”? like, if we see bot timeouts or telemetry QPS spikes, SRE can flip `telemetry.live_queries=false` first, then kill v2 if needed.

Miles Thornton: yep. ordering for rollback:
1) `incident_bot.v2.telemetry.live_queries` -> off (links only)
2) disable individual noisy card (usually saturation)
3) `incident_bot.v2.enabled` -> off (revert to v1 output)

Aisha Bello: criteria for rollback (objective):
- bot p95 time-to-first-response > 3s in #incidents for 10m
- telemetry query service error rate > 2% attributable to bot
- any redaction failure / sensitive field leak (immediate full disable + incident)
- oncall feedback: “card is wrong/misleading” (esp deploy context / canary status)

Mina Haddad: add routing safety: if v2 starts spamming wrong fallback/routing policy context, that’s dangerous. maybe gate “routing policy summary” as part of config card and keep it off until validated.

Benji Okafor: +1. we can keep routing policy summary behind config diff flag for now.

Devon Price: note: for Slack interactive actions, Slack requires ack within 3s. we should keep `interactive_actions` flag off until we’ve verified retries/idempotency. otherwise we’ll create noise.

Miles Thornton: ack. we’ll sequence rollout:
- Step 0: staging dogfood (all cards, live queries)
- Step 1: prod beta cohort: v2 enabled + deploy_context only + links-only for telemetry
- Step 2: turn on saturation_signals + live queries (still beta cohort)
- Step 3: config_diff collect_only (Slack shows “diff available” link)
- Step 4: config_diff render_in_slack for authorized users
- Step 5: expand cohort

Kaitlyn Nguyen: please ensure config_diff “collect_only” storage is access-controlled and audited. even if not in Slack, we can’t have the bot writing sensitive diffs to a broad log bucket.

Ethan Park: understood. action items:
- Ethan: create Flagger flags + ownership + default off in prod
- Miles/Devon: implement kill switch + per-card checks + links-only mode
- Kaitlyn/Benji: define config_diff flag split + confirm authz/audit requirements
- Rafael/Aisha: draft rollback criteria + playbook for #eng-oncall

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: add me on the doc, i’ll write the SRE runbook snippet.

Mina Haddad: :thumbsup: once flags exist, ping me and i’ll review the cohort expansion plan (we should include at least one platform oncall in the beta too).

Ethan Park: will do. aiming to have flags ready EOD tomorrow so we can start staging burn-in.
